entries.title: Evening Briefing · 24 November 2026
headlines: Iran claims more tankers hit mines in Hormuz; the US has not confirmed it
Nvidia gives back part of Monday's surge as chip stocks slide on Wall Street
Compass plans to move its main listing to the US; FTSE 100 edges down 0.13 percent
SP offers Congress 26 seats for Uttar Pradesh 2027; Congress wants about 130
England thrash Australia by eight wickets to level the T20I series

stories.headline: Hormuz: Iran's tanker claims remain unverified
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy and its regular navy say three tankers hit mines and caught fire east of the strait on Tuesday. Some outlets report four. US Central Command has not confirmed or denied the claim, and UKMTO has linked recent tanker incidents near Khasab to unidentified projectiles rather than mines. The US Treasury has also announced new sanctions on Iranian exchange houses and front companies.
stories.whyItMatters: Each new claim adds to the risk premium on Gulf shipping and oil. Without independent confirmation, the scale of the attacks is still unknown.

stories.headline: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills two and injures 40
stories.summary: Regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said an overnight Russian attack hit an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia city. Four children are among the 40 injured.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds to Kyiv's calls this week for more Patriot interceptors.

stories.headline: Israeli strike kills Hamas's internal security chief in Gaza
stories.summary: Medics and police in Gaza said Israeli airstrikes killed Naeem Abu Nahel, who headed Hamas's internal security apparatus, and six others, including two police officers. The Israeli military and Shin Bet said they had targeted a senior Hamas militant.
stories.whyItMatters: Targeting senior security officials puts more strain on the fragile arrangements in Gaza.

stories.headline: Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Bangladesh on 16 December
stories.summary: A spokesperson for the former prime minister, who was sentenced to death in absentia last year, said she plans to fly home and asked the government to arrange it. Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said she would be brought back in handcuffs.
stories.whyItMatters: A return would test Bangladesh's new government, and it involves India, where Hasina has been living.

stories.headline: Compass Group plans to move its primary listing to the US
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 caterer reported better-than-expected full-year results, restarted its buyback and plans to make the US its main listing, keeping London as a secondary listing. North America makes up about three-quarters of its underlying operating profit. The shares rose 4.2 percent.
stories.whyItMatters: It is another large company choosing New York over London, which adds pressure on efforts to make UK listings more attractive.

stories.headline: EU deal: a tuition fee condition, and new bills on the way
stories.summary: Reports say EU officials regard the deal signed in Brussels on Friday as dependent on the UK aligning tuition fees for EU students within six months. The government plans legislation next week for the food and drink part of the deal, and the bill setting out the wider deal is due in the Commons this week.
stories.whyItMatters: Fee alignment would affect university funding, and it gives the opposition a new line of attack before Wednesday's PMQs.

stories.headline: UP 2027: SP offers Congress 26 seats; second round ends without a deal
stories.summary: SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said the party has offered Congress 26 of the 403 seats, while Congress has listed about 130 it wants. Tuesday's seat-by-seat talks in Delhi did not reach a deal, and Yadav expects to settle it in the next two meetings. UP Congress chief Aradhana Misra said she was not aware of any 26-seat offer.
stories.whyItMatters: The gap is large, and how it closes will show whether the INDIA bloc can stay united in its biggest state contest.

stories.headline: Thirupparankundram row: lamp not lit at the hilltop pillar despite court orders
stories.summary: The Supreme Court had allowed the Karthigai deepam to be lit this year at the stone pillar on Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai. Tamil Nadu's TVK government said it was lit at the traditional spot near the Uchipillayar temple instead. BJP and Hindu groups protested, police detained cadres, and the BJP has demanded the government's dismissal.
stories.whyItMatters: The new state government is now in a direct clash with the courts over a politically sensitive religious site. A compliance report is reportedly due to the Supreme Court within three days.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office announcements today
stories.summary: GOV.UK shows no new Statement of Changes. HC 584 (3 September 2026) is still the latest, and the Home Office's most recent items, dated 23 November, are statistics and data releases. Earned settlement is government policy but is not yet in the rules. The Home Secretary said the rules would start being laid with the December changes and be phased in during 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: The announced framework makes 10 years the standard route to ILR, with 5 years for earners above 50,271 pounds and 3 years above 125,141 pounds. None of it applies until the rules are laid.

stories.headline: England beat Australia by eight wickets to level the T20I series
stories.summary: Australia made 184 for 8 on the Gold Coast, and England reached the target with 41 balls to spare. Aneurin Donald hit 85 off 32 balls and put on 151 for the first wicket with Phil Salt, who made 58.
stories.whyItMatters: The series is 1-1, with game three at the Gabba on Friday 27 November.

stories.headline: Sooryavanshi hits 204 off 53 balls as India A reach the semi-finals
stories.summary: At the Rising Stars Asia Cup in Doha, UAE made 249 for 8. India A won by seven wickets in 14.2 overs, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hitting 28 sixes in his double hundred.
stories.whyItMatters: After Sunday's loss to Pakistan A, India A needed this win and are now in the semi-finals on 26 and 27 November.

stories.headline: Champions League: Villa level at half-time in Istanbul, Arsenal and City next
stories.summary: Galatasaray and Aston Villa were 0-0 at half-time, according to live match updates. Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City v Napoli kick off at 20:00 GMT.
stories.whyItMatters: Matchday 5 of 8 decides much of the race for the top-eight places that skip the play-off round.

stories.headline: Ariane 6 launches 36 Amazon Leo satellites at the second attempt
stories.summary: Mission VA271 lifted off from Kourou at about 11:14 GMT, a day after a ground-system fault stopped Monday's countdown, and deployed all 36 satellites at about 460 km. Arianespace says it has now launched 136 Amazon Leo satellites in under 10 months.
stories.whyItMatters: Vulcan is grounded after a failure on 15 November that destroyed 40 Amazon satellites, so Ariane 6 is now a key launcher for Amazon.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 dips 0.13 percent as metals slump hits miners
stories.summary: Tuesday 24 Nov close (16:35 GMT): FTSE 100 10,467.07, down 13.75 points, and FTSE 250 down 0.8 percent. Antofagasta fell 8.1 percent, Anglo American 5.7 percent and Fresnillo 4.9 percent as gold, silver and copper slid, while Experian, Compass and RELX rose.
stories.whyItMatters: The index gave back only a small part of Monday's rebound. Investors are waiting for Wednesday's US PCE inflation data.

stories.headline: Wall Street: chips give back gains as rate-rise bets return, still trading
stories.summary: At 13:23 ET (18:23 GMT), still trading: S&P 500 7,202.38, down 0.48 percent; Dow Jones 49,997.70, up 0.81 percent; Nasdaq Composite 23,744.60, down 1.43 percent. Nvidia was down about 7 percent after Monday's 31 percent jump, and Micron and SK Hynix fell more than 10 percent, while retailers such as Dick's and Dollar Tree rose on results. Anthropic shares fell below their 83 dollar IPO price.
stories.whyItMatters: A partial reversal of Monday's huge rally shows how fragile AI-led sentiment remains ahead of inflation data.

stories.headline: Indian markets closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti; trading resumes Wednesday
stories.summary: NSE and BSE were shut on Tuesday and reopen on Wednesday 25 November. Latest figures are Monday 23 Nov closes: Sensex 82,435.99, down 1.77 percent, and Nifty 50 25,349.65, down 1.75 percent.
stories.whyItMatters: Indian stocks missed Tuesday's global moves, so Wednesday's open has to catch up.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 24 November 2026
headlines: Nvidia's 31% surge gives Wall Street its best day since April 2025
Iran claims three tankers hit mines in Hormuz, with no independent confirmation
EU proposes its 22nd Russia sanctions package, including a sports ban
Zelensky warns new Russian strikes are coming as NATO sends an AWACS to Poland
The UK will host the 2035 Women's World Cup

stories.headline: Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Late on Monday, Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said three oil tankers struck naval mines in the strait and caught fire, and that US escorts and air cover failed to stop it. It gave no ship names, flags or casualty figures. UKMTO, the US military and ship operators have not confirmed the claim. Also on Monday, the US Treasury sanctioned about two dozen Iranian front companies and exchange houses.
stories.whyItMatters: If confirmed, these would be the first hits on ships under US escort since the blockade began, a direct test of Washington's strategy and a risk to oil supplies.

stories.headline: EU proposes a 22nd sanctions package against Russia, reaching into sport
stories.summary: Ursula von der Leyen proposed cutting 60 more Russian banks off SWIFT and setting up a crypto task force on countries that help Russia get around sanctions. Russian teams and athletes would be barred from competing under the Russian flag at events in the EU. Russians who fought in Ukraine would be refused EU visas.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the EU's first sanctions move into sport and culture. All 27 member states must approve it, so one holdout could delay or weaken it.

stories.headline: Zelensky warns of new Russian strikes as NATO sends an AWACS to Poland
stories.summary: In his Monday night address, Zelensky said Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia preparing fresh strikes, and he asked partners for more air-defence missiles, especially for Patriot systems. After Monday's emergency council, NATO authorised an AWACS early-warning aircraft for Poland and said Russia bears full responsibility for the Kh-101 missiles. Poland decided not to request formal Article 4 talks.
stories.whyItMatters: Another mass strike on Ukraine looks likely within days, and NATO is strengthening its eastern flank without formal crisis talks.

stories.headline: South Korea scrambles jets as Russian warplanes enter its air defence zone
stories.summary: Early on Tuesday, Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defence identification zone near Ulleung Island, and Seoul scrambled fighters. A mistaken alert sent island residents to shelters for about three minutes and briefly said the planes were North Korean. Seoul is summoning a Russian diplomat today.
stories.whyItMatters: Russian military pressure is now being felt in East Asia as well as Europe, and the false alarm raises questions about South Korea's warning system.

stories.headline: The UK will host the 2035 Women's World Cup
stories.summary: At an online congress on Monday, FIFA approved the joint bid from England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, which was unopposed. The tournament will have 48 teams and 104 matches over 39 days. The bid proposes 22 stadiums in 16 cities, and FIFA will confirm the venues later. The 2031 tournament goes to the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the biggest football tournament in the UK since 1966. Burnham says it will bring visitors, investment and jobs, but no public funding figure has been given.

stories.headline: Finance Bill clears its first Commons vote
stories.summary: MPs gave the Finance Bill, which puts the 28 October Budget into law, a second reading just before 11pm on Monday. Reports citing the Commons division list put the vote at 311 to 164; this briefing has not checked that against the official record. The bill now goes to a committee of the whole House on 30 November and 1 December.
stories.whyItMatters: The government's tax plans cleared their first vote comfortably, with detailed scrutiny still to come.

stories.headline: Tube strike from midday on Thursday
stories.summary: The RMT has called a 24-hour Underground strike from 12:00 on Thursday 26 November to 11:59 on Friday 27 November. TfL warns that all 11 lines could be disrupted. The Elizabeth line, Overground and DLR are expected to run but will be busier. The dispute is over changes to drivers' working arrangements, and seven more strike days are planned from 17 December.
stories.whyItMatters: Anyone commuting into London on Thursday afternoon or Friday morning should plan another route.

stories.headline: Parliament passes 100 days in limbo with no Winter Session date
stories.summary: Both Houses were adjourned on 13 August, but the Monsoon Session has still not been formally ended, and no Winter Session dates have been set. Opposition leaders say the delay breaks convention. They suspect the government wants to keep the session open to retry the delimitation and women's-reservation amendment, which fell short of a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. Kiren Rijiju says the Constitution sets no deadline for prorogation.
stories.whyItMatters: When Parliament next sits, and whether that amendment returns, is the biggest open political question in Delhi.

stories.headline: Congress and SP move closer to a seat deal for Uttar Pradesh 2027
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party and Congress negotiators met in Delhi on Monday, and a second round is due today. Reports say Congress has cut its demand from 181 to about 130 of the state's 403 seats, and both sides expect a deal within two or three days once Akhilesh Yadav has reviewed the list. The seat numbers have not been officially announced.
stories.whyItMatters: The two parties fought the 2022 election separately. A deal would rebuild the main opposition alliance against the BJP in India's largest state.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks the Centre to respond on anti-defection reform
stories.summary: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notice on Monday on a petition arguing that lawmakers use tactical resignations to avoid disqualification under the Tenth Schedule. The Centre, the Election Commission, the Law Commission and two ministries must respond. No next hearing date has been set.
stories.whyItMatters: The case could tighten the rules on defections, which have repeatedly brought down state governments.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office announcements overnight
stories.summary: GOV.UK shows no new Statement of Changes; HC 584 (3 September 2026) is still the latest. The only Home Office items dated 23 November were statistics notices. Earned settlement, with 10-year ILR as the default and shorter routes for high earners, is still a proposal: rules have not been laid and there is no start date. Advisers expect rules in December. The next confirmed change is higher student maintenance funds for applications made from Monday 30 November.
stories.whyItMatters: Indian Skilled Worker visa holders and ILR applicants have no new rules to act on today.

stories.headline: Brentford beat 10-man Everton 4-0
stories.summary: Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice in quick succession midway through the first half on Monday night. Everton captain James Tarkowski was sent off on 40 minutes after a VAR review upgraded his yellow card to red. Vitaly Janelt and substitute Fabio Carvalho added the others.
stories.whyItMatters: Brentford move up to sixth in the Premier League, a point ahead of Everton, who drop to ninth.

stories.headline: Champions League: Villa, Arsenal and City in action
stories.summary: Galatasaray v Aston Villa is at 17:45 GMT. Villa are without Matty Cash and Amadou Onana, and the hosts are missing Victor Osimhen. Arsenal v Dortmund and Man City v Napoli kick off at 20:00. Enzo Maresca's City are without Antoine Semenyo. Napoli are missing several defenders, and Kevin De Bruyne and Scott McTominay return to Manchester.
stories.whyItMatters: City have taken one point from their last four league games, and a win here would steady them before Sunday's trip to Arsenal.

stories.headline: India A must beat UAE at the Rising Stars Asia Cup
stories.summary: After Sunday's 48-run loss to Pakistan A, who are through to the semi-finals, India A play UAE in Doha at 10:00 GMT (15:30 IST) needing a win to stay in contention. The semi-finals are on 26 and 27 November and the final is on 29 November.
stories.whyItMatters: If India A go through, an India-Pakistan final is still possible.

stories.headline: England chase a series-levelling win in the second T20I
stories.summary: The second of five T20Is starts at 08:15 GMT at Carrara Oval on the Gold Coast, with Australia 1-0 up. In the MCG opener, Australia chased down England's 187/9 with one ball to spare, despite 65 off 28 balls from Harry Brook.
stories.whyItMatters: England won the ODI series 2-1 and need a win today to keep pace in the T20 series.

stories.headline: Reports: Tickner out of the Christchurch Test, Fisher called up
stories.summary: New Zealand seamer Blair Tickner is reported to have hurt his right hamstring in training and to be out of the second Test against India, which starts at Hagley Oval at 22:00 GMT on Thursday. Matt Fisher reportedly joins the squad, with Tom Latham captaining. This briefing could not find New Zealand Cricket's own announcement.
stories.whyItMatters: It would leave New Zealand's attack weaker, with Mitchell Santner already injured.

stories.headline: China confirms Shenzhou-24 for 00:18 GMT on Wednesday
stories.summary: The China Manned Space Agency has confirmed the launch from Jiuquan for 08:18 Beijing time on Wednesday, which is 00:18 GMT. The crew is commander Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Ali will make a short stay and return on Shenzhou-23.
stories.whyItMatters: Ali will be Pakistan's first astronaut and the first foreign astronaut on China's Tiangong station.

stories.headline: Ariane 6 tries again today with 36 Amazon Leo satellites
stories.summary: A ground support problem stopped Monday's countdown. Arianespace has moved the launch to today, with a window from 10:45 to 11:14 GMT from Kourou. It will be the tenth Ariane 6 flight.
stories.whyItMatters: Amazon is short of rockets for its satellite network after a Vulcan failure on 15 November lost 40 of its satellites.

stories.headline: Gaganyaan G1 uncrewed flight reportedly slips to February
stories.summary: India Today, citing an unnamed senior ISRO official, reports that G1, which will carry the Vyommitra robot, is unlikely to fly before February 2027 because of extra simulations. ISRO's chairman had named December as the target on 12 November, and ISRO has not confirmed the delay.
stories.whyItMatters: India's first crewed flight, H1, cannot go until G1 has flown successfully.

stories.headline: Wall Street has its best day since April 2025
stories.summary: The S&P 500 closed up 4.73% at 7,237.17, the Dow up 3.01% (+1,447.98) at 49,595.31, and the Nasdaq Composite up 6.51% at 24,089.56. Nvidia rose about 31.5% to $165.05 after its board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO; Reuters says it was the stock's biggest one-day gain in 23 years. Dell, Micron and CoreWeave rose 15–22%, and analysts say forced buying from short-sellers covering their bets added to the gains.
stories.whyItMatters: The rally ended a run of seven straight S&P 500 losses that had pushed the indices into correction territory. It also shows how closely the AI trade is tied to one CEO.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 bounced 1.3%; Compass and Kingfisher report today
stories.summary: London closed on Monday at 10,480.82, up 134.48 points, led by tech trusts, Rolls-Royce and Standard Chartered, while Vodafone fell 5.1% after a Citi downgrade. Today brings full-year results from Compass Group, which the FT says may announce a move of its main listing to New York, plus updates from Kingfisher and AO World. Early indications point to the FTSE opening slightly higher at 08:00 GMT.
stories.whyItMatters: If Compass moves its main listing to New York, the London market loses another major company.

stories.headline: Indian markets closed today for Guru Nanak Jayanti
stories.summary: NSE and BSE are shut on Tuesday and reopen on Wednesday 25 November. On Monday, the Sensex fell 1,483.72 points (1.77%) to 82,435.99 and the Nifty 50 fell 450.95 (1.75%) to 25,349.65. Banks and metals fell most, with profit-taking near record highs, monthly F&O expiry and a rupee at about 92.85 to the dollar.
stories.whyItMatters: Indian stocks missed Monday's US tech surge, so Wednesday's open will show whether they catch up.

stories.headline: Asian chip stocks soar on the Nvidia rebound
stories.summary: Still trading: South Korea's Kospi was up 6.9% at 5,033.21 at 05:00 GMT, with Samsung and SK Hynix up about 8%, and Taiwan was up more than 9% earlier in the session. Japan's Nikkei, back from a holiday, was up 4.4% at about 02:46 GMT. Hong Kong lagged with small gains. US futures were a little higher at 06:10 GMT.
stories.whyItMatters: Asia's chipmakers had led last week's AI sell-off, so the size of today's bounce shows how quickly sentiment has turned.

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 23 November 2026
headlines: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, and Wall Street surges
FTSE 100 bounces 1.3% off its five-month low as Sensex drops 1.77%
India pledges Rs 15,000 crore to Nepal in 21 outcomes from Modi-Shah talks
Burnham tells MPs rejoining the EU is unthinkable without a referendum
Iran vows every means against the US blockade after Trump threatens to sink its ships

stories.headline: NATO council meets on the Russian missiles that hit Poland
stories.summary: The North Atlantic Council held its emergency session in Brussels on Monday, with Poland represented by deputy defence minister Pawel Zalewski. No joint statement or new decision had been reported by the evening. Allied early-warning aircraft are already reinforcing Polish airspace, and Mark Rutte said it is still being assessed whether the incursion was deliberate.
stories.whyItMatters: What allies agree for Poland's air defences will show how NATO plans to respond if Russian missiles keep straying over its eastern border.

stories.headline: Dymer rescue ends with 11 dead, including an 11-year-old girl
stories.summary: Ukraine's interior minister says the search of the collapsed block in Dymer, Kyiv region, is over after more than a day and over 2,000 tonnes of rubble cleared. Eleven people died, two are still to be identified, and five remain in hospital. A 7-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman were pulled out alive.
stories.whyItMatters: The toll adds weight to Zelensky's push for more Western air defence, including US Patriot systems.

stories.headline: Iran vows to resist the US blockade after Trump's sinking threat
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry called the US naval blockade an act of aggression and said it would use every available means against it, after Trump said ships trying to break it would go to the bottom of the sea. Iran says Hormuz could reopen quickly if sanctions and the blockade are lifted. A maritime analyst's claim that the US struck an Iranian-oil tanker has not been confirmed by either government.
stories.whyItMatters: Any clash at sea would hit oil prices and Gulf shipping, though Brent fell on Monday to about 89 dollars a barrel.

stories.headline: Burnham: rejoining the EU unthinkable without a referendum
stories.summary: In his Commons statement on last week's Brussels deal, the Prime Minister said there is a range of options for long-term ties, to be set out in his 10-year plan in mid-December. He said the deal keeps Labour's red lines on the single market, customs union and free movement. Kemi Badenoch accused him of living in the past and said prices would rise.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the clearest signal yet that Burnham will not move towards rejoining in this Parliament, though the wider debate on EU ties is still open.

stories.headline: Finance Bill debated tonight in a busy week at Westminster
stories.summary: MPs hold the Finance Bill second reading on Monday, putting the 28 October Budget into law, with rival amendments from the Conservatives and Lib Dems. PMQs is on Wednesday. The Cutting Costs Bill for the EU deal is due on Thursday, the same day the Lords debate the 20 November UK-EU summit.
stories.whyItMatters: The Budget's tax changes and the EU package both start their passage this week, so expect the main political rows here.

stories.headline: UK private-sector growth slows as services hit a five-month low
stories.summary: The S&P Global flash composite PMI eased to 52.3 in November from 52.9. Services fell to 52.0, below forecasts, while factory output reached a 27-month high. The pound slipped to about 1.302 dollars.
stories.whyItMatters: A reading above 50 still means growth, but the cooling in services will feed into Bank of England rate thinking.

stories.headline: India and Nepal agree 21 outcomes and a Rs 15,000 crore package
stories.summary: Talks between Narendra Modi and Balendra Shah ended with 21 outcomes, including a Rs 3,500 crore grant for flood-damaged hydropower and an Rs 11,500 crore credit line for energy. A new vision document allows a review of the 1950 friendship treaty by mutual consent. The leaders flagged off the Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu-Kamala Express and set a target of 10,000 MW of power imports from Nepal by 2030.
stories.whyItMatters: Delhi calls it its largest ever package for Nepal, a sign it wants close ties with Shah's new government, especially on hydropower and trade.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office announcements today
stories.summary: GOV.UK shows nothing new since Friday 20 November, when only guidance and statistics were published, and the latest Statement of Changes is still HC 584. Earned settlement has a final framework in the November government response, but no rules have been laid and there is no start date, so current ILR rules still apply. Already confirmed: higher student maintenance amounts apply to applications made from 30 November, and the Immigration and Asylum Bill is now in the Lords.
stories.whyItMatters: Indian Skilled Worker visa holders planning for ILR should watch for a new Statement of Changes, which is what would turn earned settlement into law.

stories.headline: Pakistan A beat India A by 48 runs at the Rising Stars Asia Cup
stories.summary: In Doha on Sunday, Pakistan A made 313, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring on 79. India A fell 48 runs short despite a quick 70 from Abhishek Sharma and a hundred from Tilak Varma.
stories.whyItMatters: A rare India A defeat in a high-profile game against Pakistan, with several India squad players in the side.

stories.headline: Second Test in Christchurch starts Thursday night UK time
stories.summary: After the Wellington draw, India and New Zealand meet at Hagley Oval from 27 November to 1 December. Play starts at 11am local time, so the first ball is on Thursday 26 November at 22:00 UK time.
stories.whyItMatters: With the first Test drawn, this two-match series and its World Test Championship points are decided in Christchurch.

stories.headline: Champions League matchday 5: five English clubs in action
stories.summary: Tuesday: Galatasaray v Aston Villa at 17:45 GMT, then Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City v Napoli at 20:00. Wednesday: Club Brugge v Liverpool and Sporting CP v Manchester United, both at 20:00.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the start of the second half of the league phase, when places in the top eight begin to settle.

stories.headline: NASA clears NG-25 Cygnus for Sunday, with weather the only concern
stories.summary: At Monday's preview briefing, NASA said no technical issues are being tracked for the Cygnus XL cargo ship, named S.S. James Jim Lovell. It is due to launch on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral no earlier than Sunday 29 November at 15:47 GMT with about 11,000 lb of cargo, and to be captured at the ISS on 1 December at 07:35 GMT.
stories.whyItMatters: Northrop Grumman's own Antares rocket still has no return date, so it depends on SpaceX to keep its ISS cargo flights going.

stories.headline: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang 11 days after he resigned
stories.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Huang as president and CEO with immediate effect, saying it had taken input from senior levels of the US government and was satisfied he poses no national security risk. Interim CEO Colette Kress goes back to being CFO. Nvidia has not given a reason for the 12 November resignation; a TechCrunch report linking it to a suspected Chinese spy is unconfirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: Huang's exit had driven a week-long AI sell-off, so his return is the main reason markets rebounded around the world on Monday.

stories.headline: Wall Street stages a huge AI rebound, still trading
stories.summary: At 12:33 ET (17:33 GMT), still trading, the Nasdaq Composite was up 6.90 percent at 24,178.00, the S&P 500 up 4.97 percent at 7,254.11 and the Dow up 3.19 percent at 49,684.91. Nvidia was up about 32 percent and Micron about 19 percent, with part of the move put down to short covering after seven straight days of falls.
stories.whyItMatters: Last week's rout had pushed the S&P 500 into correction. Whether the gains hold to the 21:00 GMT close will show how much of the AI selling is over.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 bounces 1.3 percent from its five-month low
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed on Monday 23 Nov (16:35 GMT) at 10,480.82, up 134.48 points or 1.3 percent, and the FTSE 250 rose 1.7 percent. Tech trusts such as Polar Capital Technology and Scottish Mortgage led, with Halma and miners. Vodafone fell 5.1 percent after a Citi downgrade, and Capita lost more than 70 percent after a profit warning and its CEO's departure.
stories.whyItMatters: It ends a five-day losing run, but London's gain was much smaller than New York's because it holds few tech stocks.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty fall 1.8 percent as banks and metals slide; markets shut Tuesday
stories.summary: Monday 23 Nov close (15:30 IST): Sensex 82,435.99, down 1,483.72 points or 1.77 percent, and Nifty 50 25,349.65, down 450.95 or 1.75 percent. Bank Nifty fell 3.17 percent and metals 3.68 percent, with Tata Steel down 8.4 percent, while IT rose 1.7 percent. Markets are closed on Tuesday 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors took profits after a four-week rally, and Indian shares will only react to Wall Street's rebound when trading resumes on Wednesday.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 23 November 2026
headlines: Russian strikes kill at least 15 across the Kyiv region
NATO meets in Brussels today as Poland says all three objects were Russian Kh-101 missiles
Asian stocks slide on the AI rout as US futures bounce about 2%
Iran claims control of Hormuz and readies 14 tankers to test the US blockade
New Zealand bat out a draw in the Wellington Test against India

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 15 across the Kyiv region
stories.summary: Overnight strikes hit several towns around Kyiv. In Dymer at least 11 people died when part of a five-storey block collapsed, with 11 still being searched for, including two children. A supermarket strike in Vyshneve killed three and injured 15, and one person died in Bila Tserkva.
stories.whyItMatters: The toll has risen sharply since yesterday's report of three deaths, as Kyiv presses Washington for more Patriot systems.

stories.headline: NATO meets today as Poland says all three objects were Kh-101 missiles
stories.summary: A preliminary finding by the Lublin prosecutor's office says the three objects that entered Polish airspace on Friday were all Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles; Warsaw first described two missiles and a drone. The North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels today, and Mark Rutte said NATO would defend every inch of Polish territory.
stories.whyItMatters: Three confirmed Russian cruise missiles on NATO soil is the most serious incursion of the war so far, and today's meeting will show how hard the alliance responds.

stories.headline: Iran claims control of Hormuz and readies 14 tankers to test the US blockade
stories.summary: Iran says ships must negotiate passage through the Strait of Hormuz with its authorities and is reported to be preparing 14 oil tankers to run the US naval blockade. Bahrain intercepted more Iranian attacks on Sunday with no new injuries, and UKMTO reported two tankers damaged. Trump said US military action would resume after the New Year unless there is a deal.
stories.whyItMatters: A tanker convoy meeting US warships is the clearest route to a direct clash and keeps an oil-price risk over markets.

stories.headline: Cutting Costs Bill heads to Parliament on Thursday
stories.summary: The bill that puts Friday's UK-EU package into law, including food-standards alignment and linking to the EU carbon market from 2028, is due before MPs on Thursday. Andy Burnham ended his European trip with talks with Dutch PM Rob Jetten. The Conservatives say the deal will raise energy bills, and universities warn about lower fees for EU students.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the first Commons test of the EU reset, and the student-fees dispute has a six-month deadline attached.

stories.headline: Modi and Nepal's Balendra Shah hold talks at Hyderabad House
stories.summary: Delegation-level talks began this morning after a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Expected outcomes include a joint vision document, MoUs on education, health, agriculture and disaster management, new connectivity and energy projects, and a virtual flag-off of the Saryu-Kamala Express. Nothing had been signed at the time of writing.
stories.whyItMatters: It is Shah's first state visit, and the deals will show how far India can rebuild ties with Nepal's new government, including flood-reconstruction aid.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules over the weekend
stories.summary: GOV.UK still lists HC 584 (3 September 2026) as the latest Statement of Changes. Earned settlement (10-year ILR) remains policy only, with no rules laid and no start date. Already confirmed: student maintenance amounts rise for applications made from 30 November, and the Immigration and Asylum Bill is now in the Lords.

stories.headline: Wellington Test drawn as New Zealand hold out
stories.summary: New Zealand finished on 239/5 after 120 overs, still 113 behind India's 720/9 declared. Daryl Mitchell (49 not out off 186 balls) and Glenn Phillips (26 not out off 126) shared an unbroken stand of 63 on a flat Basin Reserve pitch.
stories.whyItMatters: The series is level at 0-0 going into the second Test at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, from Friday 27 November.

stories.headline: Shenzhou-24 expected to fly Pakistan's first astronaut
stories.summary: China's next crewed mission is unofficially set to launch from Jiuquan at about 00:19 GMT on Wednesday 25 November, carrying a Pakistani astronaut. China has not confirmed the date; Pakistan has pointed to 25 November.
stories.whyItMatters: It would be the first foreign astronaut aboard China's Tiangong station.

stories.headline: This week: first Hera images of Dimorphos, and a Cygnus cargo launch
stories.summary: ESA releases Hera's first images of the asteroid Dimorphos on Wednesday at 18:45 GMT. NASA briefs today on the NG-25 Cygnus resupply mission, due to launch to the ISS on a Falcon 9 on Sunday 29 November at 15:49 GMT.
stories.whyItMatters: Hera is studying the asteroid NASA's DART probe struck in 2022, to measure how well the planetary-defence test worked.

stories.headline: Asia sells off on the AI rout while US futures rebound
stories.summary: Kospi fell as much as 5.8% before trading 3.2% lower at 04:30 GMT; Hong Kong and mainland China were down about 0.6%, Taiwan rose 2.5% and Japan is shut. At 02:32 GMT US futures were up: S&P 500 1.96%, Dow 1.54%, Nasdaq-100 2.33%. Friday 20 Nov closes: S&P 500 6,910.39 (down 3.70%), Dow 48,147.33 (down 1.93%), Nasdaq Composite 22,617.73 (down 5.28%).
stories.whyItMatters: Fears over AI spending, turmoil at Nvidia and bets on another Fed rate rise drove last week's losses. Brent was near 92 dollars and gold near 3,600 dollars.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty give up early gains (live, 09:46 IST)
stories.summary: Indian shares opened higher, with the Sensex up 0.78% at 84,571, then reversed. At 09:46 IST, still trading, the Sensex was down 0.64% at 83,383.75 and the Nifty 50 down 0.69% at 25,623.00, with metal and bank stocks down about 2% and IT up about 1%.
stories.whyItMatters: Friday's nine-month highs are being tested by the global tech sell-off. Some live blogs say Indian markets will be shut on Tuesday, which is not yet confirmed with the exchanges.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 starts the week at a five-month low
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed Friday 20 Nov down 1.02% at 10,346.34, its fifth straight fall and about 5% lower on the week, with miners, banks and defence stocks weakest. London opens at 08:00 GMT; firmer US futures point to a steadier start.
stories.whyItMatters: London has followed the global tech-led sell-off despite holding few tech stocks, so commodity prices and banks will set the tone today.

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 22 November 2026
headlines: COP31 collapses in Antalya with no deal after the EU, UK and island states reject a text that leaves out fossil fuels
Russian strike on a Kyiv-region apartment block kills at least three; Zelensky presses the US to release paid-for Patriot missiles
Bahrain says two people were hurt in Saturday's Iranian attacks; Iran says Hormuz could reopen if the US meets its conditions
Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United: Yoro sent off after eight minutes on Pochettino's debut
Nepal PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi; talks with Modi at Hyderabad House on Monday

stories.headline: COP31 ends without a deal after nearly two days of overtime
stories.summary: Delegates in Antalya rejected the final text at Sunday's closing plenary because it did not mention fossil fuels. The EU, the UK and small island states such as Tuvalu refused it, and COP31 president Murat Kurum said there would be no new draft. China and India objected but accepted the cover text; smaller deals on geothermal power, freight corridors and electricity were agreed.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the longest COP on record and ends without a global signal on moving away from fossil fuels. The UK delegation said it was profoundly disappointed.

stories.headline: Kyiv-region strike kills at least three as Zelensky presses the US on Patriots
stories.summary: An overnight Russian strike destroyed a section of a five-storey block in Vyshhorod district (reported as Dymer), killing at least three people and injuring four, with others trapped under rubble; the regional head reported the third body recovered at 17:46 local time. Zelensky said Russia fired about 2,700 drones, 1,460 glide bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine this week.
stories.whyItMatters: Zelensky says Patriot interceptors already paid for through NATO's PURL scheme are waiting on US approval. Air defence is Ukraine's most urgent need going into winter.

stories.headline: Bahrain: two injured in Saturday's Iranian attacks
stories.summary: Update since this morning: Bahrain's interior ministry now says two people were hurt, a Bahraini citizen who is stable and a Pakistani resident in critical condition, after a fire at an industrial site. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said reopening the Strait of Hormuz would not be difficult if the US accepts what he called reasonable conditions. Iran says talks with the US continue.
stories.whyItMatters: This morning's reports said no one was hurt. The tanker convoy at Kharg Island has not been seen moving, but a clash at sea is still the biggest risk to oil supply.

stories.headline: NATO council meets Monday on the Russian missiles in Poland
stories.summary: The North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on Monday after two Russian cruise missiles and a jet drone crossed into Poland on Friday night. New detail: a Swedish Gripen pilot under NATO command was cleared to engage a suspected Kh-101 over Poland but did not fire because the weather prevented identification.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how close NATO came to shooting at a Russian missile over allied territory, which raises the stakes for Monday's talks.

stories.headline: Israel: Eisenkot invites Likud to coalition talks
stories.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, who has the mandate to form Israel's next government, invited Netanyahu's Likud to marathon talks on a unity coalition. Earlier rounds failed to settle who would be prime minister.
stories.whyItMatters: A deal or a breakdown decides whether Israel gets a unity government or heads towards another election.

stories.headline: Burnham defends the EU deal as Tories and universities raise costs
stories.summary: The government's Cutting Costs Bill, which puts Friday's Brussels package into law, is due in Parliament on Thursday. The Conservatives say joining the EU carbon market will push up fuel and gas bills, which ministers call completely wrong. Universities warn that charging EU students home fees, which must happen within six months, could leave a funding gap.
stories.whyItMatters: Thursday's bill is the first parliamentary test of the reset, and costs to households and universities will decide the political argument.

stories.headline: Rejoin row: Johnson and Cameron join May in warning Burnham
stories.summary: Update since this morning: Boris Johnson and David Cameron also warned against reopening EU membership. Europe minister Hamish Falconer said there would be a general election before any long-term decision on rejoining. Alex Burghart said the Conservatives would repeal the deal, and Kemi Badenoch asked why no treaty text has been published.
stories.whyItMatters: Three former prime ministers now oppose rejoin talk, and the opposition has promised to undo the deal, so the reset is set to be an election issue.

stories.headline: Two Gwent Police officers sacked over the St Mellons crash inquiry
stories.summary: A misconduct panel dismissed PC Richard Hardwick and PC Lauren Livingstone without notice on Friday. It found they failed to search homes during the missing-persons inquiry linked to the fatal March 2023 St Mellons crash in Cardiff and then lied about it. Other officers face proceedings later.
stories.whyItMatters: Families have long criticised the police response to the crash, and more misconduct cases are still to come.

stories.headline: Nepal PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi
stories.summary: Shah landed on Sunday for a two-day state visit and was received by minister of state Jitin Prasada; S Jaishankar called on him in the evening. Delegation talks with Modi at Hyderabad House on Monday are due to be followed by a joint press statement, a joint vision document and several agreements.
stories.whyItMatters: Reports say the 669 MW Lower Arun hydropower project and a Janakpur to Ayodhya train may be launched, but neither government has confirmed this.

stories.headline: India and China hold corps commander talks on the Arunachal frontier
stories.summary: A second round of corps commander talks on the eastern frontier, led on India's side by Lt Gen Girish Kalia of III Corps, ran for about ten days from 8 November. The aim is to prevent clashes and agree rules of engagement for patrols before winter.
stories.whyItMatters: Neither side has announced an agreement or a timeline, so it is unclear when any new rules would take effect.

stories.headline: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies at 72
stories.summary: Wadkute died of cardiac arrest at AIIMS New Delhi after being admitted on 20 November. He was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April, and Modi sent condolences.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules today
stories.summary: No new Statement of Changes and no new Home Office or UKVI announcement since Friday; Friday's GOV.UK items were caseworker guidance and data only. Earned settlement (10-year ILR) is still a policy with no rules laid and no start date. Student maintenance amounts rise for applications made from 30 November, eight days away.
stories.whyItMatters: For Indian Skilled Workers heading for ILR, the current five-year rules still apply; the December Statement of Changes is the one to watch.

stories.headline: Immigration and Asylum Bill clears the Commons
stories.summary: The Home Office says the bill passed its third reading in the Commons on 18 November and now goes to the House of Lords. On 19 November the Home Secretary also welcomed a new chair of the Migration Advisory Committee.
stories.whyItMatters: The bill is not law yet. The MAC advises on salary thresholds and visa lists, so its new chair matters for future Skilled Worker changes.

stories.headline: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United
stories.summary: Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes for bringing down Alexander Isak, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the free kick. Florian Wirtz added a second soon after, then Rio Ngumoha (66) and Victor Munoz (82) completed the win at Anfield.
stories.whyItMatters: It was a heavy defeat in Pochettino's first game; United stay in the relegation zone with 8 points from 11 games, and Liverpool move to 21.

stories.headline: Hull 2-0 Brighton with two late McBurnie goals
stories.summary: Oli McBurnie scored twice in stoppage time after Brighton's Costinha was sent off on 89 minutes for a second yellow card. It was Hull's first home win since August.
stories.whyItMatters: Brighton missed the chance to cut Arsenal's lead to three points, so the leaders stay six clear.

stories.headline: Wellington Test: India need eight wickets on day five
stories.summary: New Zealand resume on 119/2, still 233 behind India's 720/9 declared. Play starts at 22:00 GMT tonight.
stories.whyItMatters: A win would put India 1-0 up in the two-Test series.

stories.headline: SpaceX launches NROL-136 spy satellites from California
stories.summary: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg at about 04:23 Pacific time (about 12:23 GMT) carrying satellites for the US National Reconnaissance Office. The booster, on its 14th flight, landed back at Vandenberg, about 32 hours after the previous launch from the same pad.
stories.whyItMatters: Fast turnarounds on one pad show how quickly the US is building its new constellation of reconnaissance satellites.

stories.headline: Wall Street: Friday close, markets shut today
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (16:00 ET): S&P 500 down 3.70 percent at 6,910.39, Dow down 1.93 percent at 48,147.33 and Nasdaq Composite down 5.28 percent at 22,617.73. Nvidia fell 14 percent after a report of an SEC accounting review, and Fed signals pointed to more rate rises.
stories.whyItMatters: The S&P 500 and Dow are in correction, and futures price a high chance of a Fed rise on 8 to 9 December. US futures reopen at 23:00 GMT tonight.

stories.headline: FTSE 100: Friday close at a five-month low
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (16:35 GMT): FTSE 100 down 1.02 percent at 10,346.34, its fifth fall in a row and about 5 percent lower on the week. Miners fell with copper, and banks and defence stocks also dropped.
stories.whyItMatters: UK PMI data on Monday is the next test for London shares.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty: Friday close at nine-month highs
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (15:30 IST): Sensex up 1.08 percent at 83,919.71 and Nifty 50 up 1.12 percent at 25,800.60, led by banks, as foreign investors kept buying.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a short week: Indian markets are closed on Tuesday 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
